liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Crazy Fingers** (2 reviews): Start sounds as if Garcia forgot the song; the ending sounds awesome; A tease of The Other One came before it, which the reviewer loved [11][12]
- **Terrapin Station** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls it their worst ever: Garcia skips two verses, then repeats an earlier verse and abandons it; Lyrics were among the worst, but the transition from Lady with a Fan was delicate and fluid [8][10]
- **Morning Dew** (2 reviews): Sung very well, and the band sounded energized from Space onward; Garcia shouted the 'doesn't matter' line eight or nine times over the rising build-up [9][10]
- **Johnny B. Goode** (2 reviews): Closing encore was a rocking finish and the song's final appearance, per the reviewer; Reviewer waved goodbye during it, knowing it was their final show [7][17]
- **Eternity** (1 review): Reviewer considers it one of the best versions ever [12]
- **It's All Too Much** (1 review): Sounded to the reviewer like an unrehearsed garage band attempting a Beatles cover [8]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Singled out as especially hot within a strong second set [7]
- **The Other One** (1 review): A solid nine-minute jam, uncommon for 1995 [9]

## Setlist highlights

- **It's All Too Much**: rare: 6 archived performances [18]

## The recordings

- **gd95-03-26.sbd.3909.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 19 songs; 155 min; rated 3.09/5 by 22 [1]. Said about its sound: Soundboard quality is good and very forward, though Garcia's playing is sloppy in places [9]
- **gd1995-03-26.sbd.tetzeli.fix-3909.34935.shnf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 155 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [2]
- **gd1995-03-26.152479.aud-unknown-onemoreshot.shnf**: audience recording; 18 songs; 149 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [4]. Said about its sound: On Morning Dew, the uploader preferred the sound of the other audience recordings [4]
- **gd1995-03-26.141195.FOB-mk4.ebel.flac1644**: source not stated; 18 songs; 158 min [3]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended but skipped the first set because a hungover travel companion made them late [6]
- Reviewer's only Dead show; they spent eleven years looking for a listenable copy [14]
- Second set had a groovy, relaxed yet upbeat mood in the arena [16]
- Reviewer's last of over 100 shows; the band seemed small and low-energy compared with the 1980s [17]
- Reviewer rates the second-set jam among the best of 1995, one that truly clicked [6]
- Ranked among the best 1995 shows, alongside 2/21 and 3/23, with the band playing well [7]
- Reviewer considers it one of the more off nights of 1995, a two-star show [11]
- One of the few good nights of Spring Tour 1995, played with cohesion and confidence [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd95-03-26.sbd.3909.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by c. ladner; source: SBD > MC > DAT > CDR [1]. Also: Soundboard to MC to DAT to CDR; seeded via cm, extracted with EAC and SHNv3 by c. ladner [1]
- **gd1995-03-26.sbd.tetzeli.fix-3909.34935.shnf**: transferred by Chris Ladner and Bill Tetzeli; source: SBD > MC > DAT [2]. Also: Bill made the CD 2 to CD 3 transition seamless, cleaning errors with shntool and merging the drums outro track; Charlie Miller supplied the overlap between the two CDs that enabled the fix [2]
- **gd1995-03-26.152479.aud-unknown-onemoreshot.shnf**: source: Audience downloaded from a.b.m.s 07/03; [4]
- **gd1995-03-26.141195.FOB-mk4.ebel.flac1644**: transferred by Pete Ebel; source: flac16/44.1khz Source Info:FOB Schoeps MK 4->Reutelhuber P/S-> Teac DA-P20-> DATTransfer Info:Dat Tape (Panasonic SV-3700)-> Marantz CDR-615-> CD (Late… [3]
